compiled_kernel_resources.scope: Static compiler declarations, not measured occupancy.

machine_code_diagnostic.scope: Read-only disassembly of all eight scalar/vector producer kernels in the measured executable. Opcode counts and resource declarations are static observations and do not independently isolate a performance cause.

implementation: Add an optional VectorLoads template route, default false, to existing C64 and whole-dot producers. Cache each immutable source-row eligibility value and row pointer before K. Load a complete32-byte K16 representation with memcpy; use an alignment assumption only after checking the actual source address, retaining ordinary memcpy for any misaligned row. Inactive rows return a zero vector before address calculation. Keep the original default scalar load loops, matrix operands, zero-C operations, explicit sums, envelopes, compaction and exact continuation arithmetic. No production dispatcher opts in. Source operands and flags must be immutable for the launch.
correctness_scope: Host sanitizers check1048576 copied words covering all65536 BF16 encodings,64 exact allocation tails and null inactive rows with zero/maximum offsets. The complete local suite reruns envelope and canonical tests. Native eleven fixtures include independent and simultaneous misalignment, short/odd K16 tails, zeros, cancellation and unsupported inputs. Each of five producer/replay configurations runs scalar and vector loading. Raw center/interval equality, candidate counts, continuation counts and total executed groups must match across loading modes; all GB10 BF16 outputs, complete replay raw endpoints, continuation membership/carry, source/prepared words, metadata bounds/audit immutability, redzones and unused tails are checked. References remain comparison inputs only; repeated fixture CPU counts are deduplicated. Native arithmetic error assumptions are unchanged.
timing_scope: Ten configurations combine scalar/vector loads with C64/full replay, whole-dot/full replay, whole-dot snapshot/full replay, two-stage and four-stage exact continuation. One warmup and three completed host samples rotate whole-owner order by three positions. Include lossless preparation, eligibility, quarter metadata when applicable, producer, compaction/count reads and complete replay/continuation work. Allocation, resetting, canonical/reference work, checks and separate audits are excluded; both loading modes reserve identical maximum workspaces. Misaligned cases are generated correctness probes. Captured q8192 repeats1023 q7169 rows and is not a token loop. C64 QKV is a slower control than the retained QKV matrix producer.

decision.retain_as: Validated optional operand-transport primitive and isolated component route; not product or release qualification.
decision.reason: All generated, captured GB10, raw center/error and continuation-work checks pass. Vector loads reduce the complete C64 OUT median by8.3443ms and QKV by19.4404ms in this experiment; all whole-dot variants improve against their scalar-load counterpart but remain slower than vector C64. The unchanged captured QKV C64 control remains slower than the retained QKV producer, so no QKV producer replacement follows from these results.
decision.next_step: Port the bounded vector read to the actual ordered K16 M64 projection producer and the existing coarse OUT owner behind a default-off switch; compare unchanged raw operands/results, then measure the full q8192/out512 model with the attached GB10 continuation.
limitations: Captured q8192 uses the established repeated-row extension and is not a token loop.
Static VGPR and opcode counts are diagnostic; they do not establish occupancy or isolate a runtime cause.
The native matrix error assumption is unchanged and is not a hardware proof.
Three samples in one process do not establish long-term performance stability.
